history.heading: Norman heritage
paragraphs: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, located off the coast of Normandy. The Bailiwick of Guernsey also includes Alderney, Sark, Herm and smaller islands. The islands were part of the Duchy of Normandy, and when King John lost mainland Normandy to France in 1204, the islands chose to remain loyal to the English crown.
Victor Hugo lived in exile in Guernsey from 1855 to 1870 and wrote Les Misérables there.

history.heading: German occupation
paragraphs: The Channel Islands were the only part of the British Isles occupied by Germany during the Second World War, from 1940 to 1945. Many children were evacuated to England, and the Germans built extensive fortifications. Liberation Day, 9 May, is the island's national day.

culture.heading: Island identity
paragraphs: English is the main language, while Guernésiais, a form of Norman French, is spoken by a small number of people and is being revived. Guernsey is famous for its Guernsey cattle and milk, and the Guernsey sweater. Gâche, a fruit bread, and bean jar are traditional foods.

politics.heading: Crown Dependency
paragraphs: Guernsey is a British Crown Dependency, not part of the United Kingdom. It is self-governing, with its own parliament, the States of Deliberation, laws and tax system, while the UK is responsible for defence and international representation. Alderney and Sark have their own legislatures.

economy.heading: Finance
paragraphs: Financial services, including banking, fund management and insurance, dominate the economy, supported by low taxes. Tourism, horticulture and e-commerce also contribute. The Guernsey pound is at par with the British pound.
